subject.title: [Bug] Dashboard Stop button can corrupt session files + agent permission isolation lacks guardrails

question: Should #91440 remain the umbrella for both Stop/session durability and host-exec isolation, and what default host-exec boundary should existing users get?
rationale: Current code and docs show the Stop durability work is partly mitigated but not live-proven, while default host exec is an intentional trusted-operator product/security stance; automation should not choose that boundary silently.

options.title: Split Lifecycle And Exec Policy
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella, split focused child work for Stop durability/recovery and host-exec isolation, and require maintainer security review before changing defaults.

options.title: Narrow To Stop Durability
options.body: Scope this issue to Dashboard Stop/session recovery and open a separate security-policy issue for per-agent exec isolation and destructive-command guardrails.

options.title: Keep Trusted Exec Default
options.body: Treat current host-exec defaults as intended, document/doctor the hardened profile path, and only fix the Stop/session data-loss surface here.

recommendation.title: Split Lifecycle And Exec Policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella, split focused child work for Stop durability/recovery and host-exec isolation, and require maintainer security review before changing defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the best current routing candidate from the inspected history for the abort/session and exec-default surfaces touched by this decision.
